42609486.exclusion_reason: no trained model stated (GLM and ICA analyses only, no machine learning classifier)

42626602.clinical_problem: classification of adolescent major depressive disorder subgroups by sleep symptom burden using resting-state fMRI connectivity
42626602.patient_population: First-episode, drug-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder (162, split into higher and lower sleep-symptom-burden groups) plus 53 healthy adolescent controls
42626602.model_description: Exploratory SVM models were trained on voxel-wise default mode network (DMN) homogeneity values derived from resting-state fMRI to distinguish adolescents with major depressive disorder (higher vs. lower sleep symptom burden) from healthy controls. The abstract reports only modest discriminative performance, indicating limited individual-level classification utility.
42626602.dataset_size: 162 adolescents with MDD (86 higher sleep-symptom-burden, 76 lower) and 53 healthy controls
42626602.headline_result: Exploratory SVM analyses showed modest discriminative performance, indicating limited utility of network homogeneity alterations alone for individual-level classification.
42626602.study_design: cross-sectional case-control resting-state fMRI study with exploratory SVM classification

42640475.model_family: data-driven clustering with machine learning classification
42640475.clinical_problem: identifying molecular subtypes of adolescent major depressive disorder from brain connectome to improve case-control discrimination
42640475.model_description: Individualized edge-centric functional brain connectomes were derived from MRI and used to compute nodal entropy per region; a data-driven clustering algorithm identified two adolescent MDD subtypes, and machine learning models were then built to test whether subtype division improved case-control discrimination. Subtype-specific entropy patterns were further linked to transcriptomic and neurotransmitter profiles.
42640475.headline_result: Subtype-based models significantly improved case-control discriminability, with the two subtypes characterized by distinct core predictive factors.
42640475.study_design: cross-sectional case-control connectomics study with unsupervised subtyping and machine learning classification

emb:L2048239924.clinical_problem: classification of second-language literacy acquisition stage from fMRI activation patterns
emb:L2048239924.patient_population: Native Mandarin-speaking children at three stages of second-language (English) literacy acquisition: pre-readers, beginning readers, and advanced readers
emb:L2048239924.model_description: fMRI was collected while native Mandarin-speaking children at different stages of learning to read English (L2) passively viewed L1 and L2 words. A supervised machine learning classifier used visual word form area activation patterns to discriminate the three L2 literacy-acquisition groups; L2-based activation, but not L1-based activation, reliably separated the groups.
emb:L2048239924.headline_result: Supervised machine learning successfully discriminated among the three L2 literacy groups using L2 (but not L1) activation patterns.
emb:L2048239924.study_design: cross-sectional fMRI study with supervised machine learning classification

emb:L2046229416.exclusion_reason: systematic review of AI tools for youth mental health prediction broadly across many non-imaging input types; not specific to radiology/neuroimaging (only a small MRI-based ASD subset)

emb:L2047523844.model_family: deep neural networks vs. simple demographic models (comparative benchmarking)
emb:L2047523844.clinical_problem: benchmarking AI prediction of psychiatric phenotypes from neuroimaging versus demographic confounds in youth
emb:L2047523844.patient_population: Youth from a large developmental clinical cohort, evaluated for diverse psychiatric and non-psychiatric phenotypes using EEG and fMRI
emb:L2047523844.model_description: Machine learning models, including deep neural networks, were trained on EEG and fMRI data from a large youth developmental cohort to predict psychiatric and non-psychiatric phenotypes. Their performance was compared against simple models using only demographics and recording site; imaging-based models did not outperform the demographic-only models for clinical phenotypes.
emb:L2047523844.headline_result: Simple models using only demographics and recording site matched deep neural network performance using EEG/fMRI data for clinical phenotype prediction.
emb:L2047523844.study_design: retrospective benchmarking study of machine learning models on a developmental neuroimaging cohort

emb:L2047521832.exclusion_reason: no trained model stated (neural decoding described without naming a specific trained/evaluated classifier)

emb:L2045170835.model_family: machine learning classifier (unspecified) on structural MRI volumetric features
emb:L2045170835.clinical_problem: classification of adolescent offender status from structural brain volumetry
emb:L2045170835.patient_population: Male adolescents 14-18 years old in conflict with the law: 19 offenders and 21 non-offenders
emb:L2045170835.model_description: Structural MRI-derived regional brain volumes (including globus pallidus and cerebellar lobules) were used as input to a machine learning classifier to distinguish adolescent offenders from non-offenders. The volumetric features showed only modest discriminative ability (balanced accuracy approximately 0.78), and the authors caution against causal interpretation.
emb:L2045170835.headline_result: Machine learning analyses indicated volumetric features contain modest discriminative information between groups (balanced accuracy approximately 0.78).
emb:L2045170835.study_design: cross-sectional case-control structural MRI study with machine learning classification

emb:L2045628810.model_family: machine learning model with PCA-derived whole-brain predictors
emb:L2045628810.clinical_problem: prediction of children's literacy (reading, verbal, naming) skills from task-based fMRI activation
emb:L2045628810.patient_population: School-aged children, 6.7-10.3 years, in subgroups of 73-97 completing different fMRI tasks
emb:L2045628810.model_description: Whole-brain activation contrast maps from four task-based fMRI paradigms (a phonological-lexical decision task, audiovisual character learning, and two passive viewing tasks) were reduced with principal component analysis and used in a machine learning model to predict continuous reading, verbal, and naming scores in school-aged children. Active tasks (phonological-lexical decision, character learning) outperformed passive viewing tasks for prediction.
emb:L2045628810.dataset_size: Subgroups of 73-97 children per fMRI task
emb:L2045628810.headline_result: Highest predictive performance for Reading and Naming scores was with the phonological-lexical decision task, outperforming character-learning and passive viewing tasks.
emb:L2045628810.study_design: cross-sectional task-based fMRI study with machine learning prediction of behavioral scores

emb:L2045628495.clinical_problem: deriving brain-based markers of adolescent phenotypic (personal, social, neighborhood) variation from structural MRI
emb:L2045628495.patient_population: Adolescents with longitudinal structural MRI data
emb:L2045628495.model_description: A convolutional neural network was trained on longitudinal structural MRI data to derive latent, low-dimensional brain representations capturing structural variability during adolescence. These learned representations were used to map associations between brain structure and personal, social, and neighborhood conditions.
emb:L2045628495.study_design: longitudinal structural MRI study using a convolutional neural network for representation learning

emb:L2044847347.clinical_problem: differentiating ADHD, ASD, and typically developing children using brain connectivity signatures
emb:L2044847347.patient_population: Children with ADHD, ASD, and typically developing controls (fMRI n=549, MEG n=215)
emb:L2044847347.model_description: A deep neural mapping model was applied to resting-state fMRI and MEG functional connectivity matrices from children with ADHD, ASD, and typically developing controls. The model extracted low-dimensional latent embeddings of connectivity patterns and aligned them with clinical symptom scores to reveal shared and disorder-specific network signatures distinguishing the groups.
emb:L2044847347.headline_result: Typically developing children clustered more closely with the ADHD group than the ASD group; MEG-derived embeddings showed stronger associations with symptom dimensions than fMRI.
emb:L2044847347.study_design: cross-sectional multimodal (fMRI/MEG) connectivity study using deep learning representation learning

emb:L2045627084.model_family: machine learning on multiscale-entropy functional brain network features
emb:L2045627084.clinical_problem: predicting adolescents' disposition to transcendent thinking from nonlinear resting-state fMRI brain dynamics
emb:L2045627084.patient_population: Diverse sample of adolescents with resting-state fMRI
emb:L2045627084.model_description: Resting-state fMRI was used to build nonlinear functional brain networks based on multiscale entropy (MSE) similarity between regions; graph-theoretical, spectral, and information-theoretic features were computed and fed into machine learning models to predict adolescents' disposition toward transcendent thinking, compared against conventional linear connectivity-based networks.
emb:L2045627084.headline_result: MSE-based network features (particularly spectral energy and Shannon entropy) reliably predicted transcendent thinking, while conventional time-series-based network measures did not; no features predicted IQ.
emb:L2045627084.study_design: cross-sectional resting-state fMRI study with machine learning prediction of a psychological trait

emb:L2044625849.model_family: machine learning combined with canonical correlation analysis
emb:L2044625849.body_region: white matter tracts (48 tracts, whole brain)
emb:L2044625849.clinical_problem: relating white matter geometric development to executive function and crystallised intelligence
emb:L2044625849.patient_population: 598 participants, ages 67-263 months (about 5.6-22 years), from the Human Connectome Project
emb:L2044625849.model_description: Diffusion MRI from 598 participants aged 5.6-22 years was analyzed with director field analysis to quantify tract-level splay, bend, twist, and distortion across 48 white matter tracts. Canonical correlation analysis and machine learning related these geometric features to cognition, finding that patterns in the cingulum and internal capsule predicted individual differences in executive function and crystallised intelligence.
emb:L2044625849.headline_result: Canonical correlation analysis (r = 0.60-0.64) and machine learning showed geometric patterns, particularly in the cingulum and internal capsule, predicted individual differences in executive function and crystallised intelligence.
emb:L2044625849.study_design: cross-sectional diffusion MRI study with machine learning and canonical correlation analysis

emb:L2044875933.exclusion_reason: no trained model stated (region-of-interest and activation contrast analyses only, no machine learning classifier)

emb:L2039950986.clinical_problem: predicting depression and anxiety severity in adolescents from resting-state fMRI intrinsic neural timescale
emb:L2039950986.patient_population: Adolescents with major depressive disorder and healthy controls
emb:L2039950986.model_description: Resting-state fMRI was used to compute cortical intrinsic neural timescale (INT), a measure of temporal stability of neural activity, in adolescents with major depressive disorder and healthy controls. An SVR-based machine learning model used INT patterns to predict individual depression and anxiety severity scores; INT alterations were also linked to suicidal ideation and childhood trauma.
emb:L2039950986.headline_result: SVR-based machine learning showed altered intrinsic neural timescale patterns predicted individual depression and anxiety severity.
emb:L2039950986.study_design: cross-sectional resting-state fMRI case-control study with SVR-based prediction

emb:L2039217866.model_family: machine learning predictor analysis on graph-theoretic functional connectome measures
emb:L2039217866.clinical_problem: predicting longitudinal functional brain network development in mid-adolescents from social circumstances and psychological disposition
emb:L2039217866.patient_population: Mid-adolescents from low-socioeconomic-status contexts followed longitudinally with fMRI (n=65)
emb:L2039217866.model_description: Longitudinal (2-year) resting-state fMRI graph-theory metrics were computed to characterize functional brain network (FBN) development in mid-adolescents. Machine learning analysis identified transcendent thinking (a psychological disposition) and community violence exposure, but not IQ, as the principal predictors of FBN change, with effects differing by parental education and violence exposure subgroup.
emb:L2039217866.headline_result: Machine learning identified transcendent thinking and community violence exposure, but not IQ, as principal predictors of functional brain network change.
emb:L2039217866.study_design: longitudinal resting-state fMRI study with machine learning predictor analysis

emb:L2038321162.model_family: explainable AI / machine learning on multimodal neuroimaging and multilevel factors
emb:L2038321162.clinical_problem: predicting early adolescent alcohol use (sipping) trajectories from multimodal brain imaging and multilevel risk factors
emb:L2038321162.patient_population: Youth from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study followed for alcohol sipping behavior
emb:L2038321162.model_description: Machine learning (explainable AI) models combined multilevel individual, family, and environmental factors with multimodal MRI features (brain structure and functional connectivity) from the ABCD Study to prospectively predict early alcohol sipping trajectories in youth. Structural and functional connectivity features distinguished youth with increasing alcohol sipping trajectories from those who reduced or did not engage in drinking.
emb:L2038321162.headline_result: Functional connectivity and structural MRI features, combined with multilevel factors, distinguished youth with increasing versus non-increasing alcohol sipping trajectories over time.
emb:L2038321162.study_design: longitudinal cohort study (ABCD) with explainable machine learning prediction of substance-use trajectories

emb:L2038292821.exclusion_reason: no trained model stated (drift-diffusion behavioral model and fMRI activation analyses only, no image-based machine learning classifier)
